title: Love
hook: above all these, put on love
tomorrow: what do you leave someone when you have nothing to leave?

segments.voice: Last week ended in a garden: an honest ask, then thy will. A new week, and it starts with getting dressed.

Seven in the morning. An old man sits on the edge of the bed, one sock on, the other out of reach. His granddaughter kneels and works it over his heel while he grumbles about the cane by the door. Shirt, buttons, cane: one more thing to wear. Paul wrote a getting-dressed list too, in his letter to the Colossians, piece by piece: mercy, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering. Then he names the last layer, the one that goes on over everything.
screen: `ONE SOCK ON.` → `ONE MORE THING TO WEAR.` → `PAUL'S WARDROBE.`

segments.voice: Here it is: “And above all these things put on charity, which is the bond of perfectness.” Charity is the King James word for love. A bond is what ties things together. So love isn't one more item on the pile; it holds the others in place. Kindness without love can turn cold. Patience without love turns into gritted teeth. Look at the verb, too: put on. Paul writes as if love can be chosen, like a coat in the morning: not only felt, but worn on purpose, even on days the feeling is thin. Just before this, he shows where it gets worn: “Forbearing one another, and forgiving one another.” Love in Colossians lives in households and kitchens, among people who annoy each other, at the edge of a bed with a sock in hand. Where does it start? The first letter of John answers: “We love him, because he first loved us.” Love begins by being loved. And Jesus gives it as his own commandment: “That ye love one another, as I have loved you.” As I have loved you. The measure is his.
screen: `THE LAST LAYER: CHARITY.` · `PUT ON, LIKE A COAT.` · `WORN AT HOME.` · `LOVED FIRST.` · then, large: `ABOVE ALL, LOVE.`

segments.voice: Write one name on a scrap of paper: someone you'll see soon. Under it, write one plain way to love them well today: listening without fixing, a task taken off their hands, a kind word said out loud. If you pray, hold them before God by name.
Love. The bond that holds every other virtue together: put on by choice, and rooted in being loved first.
Your line: above all, love. The last layer, worn even when the feeling is thin. Day seventeen forty-four.

screen: `DAY 1744 COUNTS.` → `LIVING IT · 63 OF 70.` → `TOMORROW: WHAT DO YOU LEAVE WHEN YOU HAVE NOTHING TO LEAVE?`

howItsDone: Christians speak of love as the heart of Jesus' commandments, and practice it in households, churches and service to neighbors.

chat.meaning: Paul says “put on charity”: love chosen and worn on purpose, the bond over every other virtue. It counts on the thin-feeling days too.
